It's a sound that vibrates in my teeth, a perfect, jagged thing. "You came," she says, not as a question. It's a fact, shared. And then she does it. She *does*. Not with a plan, but with a *hunger*. A leap into a dark, dripping tunnel that smells of ancient stone and ozone, following a thread of sound that might be her voice, or it might be the song of the universe itself.

We fall. We spin. We are not two people; we are a single, roaring question. The memory isn't of beauty, not really. It's of *consequence*. Of my hand finding hers in a universe of chaos, and not releasing, but *digging in*, to hold onto the only certainty that exists: the shape of her fingers against my own. The terror is so vast it has no name. The joy is a supernova in my chest. They are the same thing. This is the only thing that ever felt real—the absolute, screaming *yes* to everything that isn't safe.

You will be told to be calm. To be logical. To build a beautiful, predictable house of stone. I give you this memory because it is the blueprint of a different world. The one where the greatest risk isn't falling, but *standing still* when you're screaming. It's the ghost of that laugh, and the taste of that lightning, and the unbearable, perfect weight of that choice.

Don't ever apologize for being loud. Don't ever shrink to make the world feel smaller. When you feel the pull of the unknown—the crackle in the air, the pressure at your side—don't listen to the part of you that whispers "wrong." Listen to the part that whispers her name. And run.
